outcome: Primary clinical success rate of PAE
cohort: The study included 68 patients who underwent 74 pelvic artery embolization (PAE) procedures for obstetric hemorrhage between January 2003 and January 2013 at three tertiary care centers.
finding: Pelvic artery embolization (PAE) is an effective treatment for obstetric hemorrhage with a low complication rate and preserves fertility, and its failure is significantly associated with hemodynamic instability, hemoglobin level <95 g/dL, and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC).
